rv.q: It is, however, a balm to the soul as much as a workout for the brain, and its current Off Broadway revival reminds us why this 1993 play about what’s lost to time has, so far, proven timeless.

The flow of movement does have some life and interest to it, and it shows the company to its best advantage — and yet, as the devastating and gorgeous climax approaches, there’s too little precision, and therefore too little real pathos, for our hearts to receive the blow.
Bedlam’s production shows that it’s a gold mine of emotion and ideas, nowhere near tapped-out.
The off-putting histrionics overshadow Stoppard’s intellectual points.
Bedlam's revival is an object lesson in what happens when those involved lack the artistic strength to squeeze the nutcracker all the way.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Bedlam's stripped-down revival of Stoppard's cerebral masterpiece. While some praise the excellent interpretation and bold choices, others find the production's unconventional approach weakens the play's impact.
